Players.Name: Amy Jones
Players.DidyouKnow: Amy Jones is a former MCC Young Cricketer.
Players.Bio:
Wicketkeeper batswoman Amy Jones came in as a replacement for former cricketer Sarah Taylor, making her international debut against Sri Lanka in the 2013 ICC Women's World Cup. Her T20I debut came later the same year against Pakistan.

Her formative years in domestic cricket saw her represent the English Academy as well as Warwickshire.

Jones had an impressive outing at the 2018 T20 World Cup, with her unbeaten 53 against India being one of the highlights.

The Perth Scorchers welcomed her to the Big Bash League, signing her up for the 2018-19 season. Her debut in the league saw her smash 57 off just 29 deliveries.

Jones took over the gloves full-time for England following Taylor's retirement, while remaining a regular face in the WBBL, playing for both the Scorchers and Sydney Thunder.

More than a decade into her international career, Jones struck her first ODI century against West Indies in June 2025, then backed it up with a second a game later.

That form saw her in demand at the WBBL|11 draft, where she was snapped up by the Melbourne Stars.

Players.Name: Meg Lanning
Players.DidyouKnow: Lanning scored an unbeaten century in just her second international match against England in 2011.
Players.Bio:
Meg Lanning is a cricket superstar.

A seven-times World Cup winner, five of them as captain - and Commonwealth Games gold medallist - Lanning wasted no time when she burst onto the international scene as a teenager in 2010, scoring a century against England in just her second ODI.

Two years later, she set a new benchmark for fastest one-day ton by an Aussie, slamming a 45-ball hundred against New Zealand at North Sydney Oval in a record that stood until Glenn Maxwell beat it during the 2023 men's ODI World Cup.

In January 2014, Lanning became Australia's youngest-ever captain, standing in for an injured Jodie Field during the Ashes, and a month later was appointed full-time skipper of the T20 side.

She led her team to victory in the T20 World Cup in Bangladesh later the same year, and after assuming the Test and ODI captaincies in 2015, helped Australia win back the women's Ashes for the first time since 2001.

Lanning endured a tough 2017, undergoing a shoulder reconstruction shortly after her team's shock exit from the ODI World Cup.

But the Australia captain emerged better than ever before, leading the charge into a golden new era that saw Australia win the 2018 and 2020 T20 World Cups, the 2022 one-day World Cup, claim a world record 26 ODI victories in a row and continue to keep the Ashes out of English hands, before making history when she led Australia to gold as women's T20 cricket made its Commonwealth Games debut.

Lanning also continues to rewrite the record books; she has struck more one-day tons than any other woman and is Australia's all-time leading run scorer across all formats.

She took a six-month break from cricket following the Commonwealth Games, but returned to lead Australia to the 2023 T20 World Cup in South Africa, which was her final appearance in Australian gold. 

Lanning announced her retirement from international cricket in November 2023, but continues to play domestic cricket in the WBBL and WNCL.

Players.Name: Carly Leeson
Players.Bio:
Born in Grafton, NSW, Carly Leeson represented New South Wales at under-15 and under-18 level and was a member of the Shooting Stars squad that toured Sri Lanka in 2015.

Leeson signed with the Sydney Sixers ahead of WBBL|02 in 2016–17, debuting against the Melbourne Renegades.

She spent three seasons with the club before moving to the Renegades ahead of WBBL|05, where she remained until her contract was not renewed at the end of WBBL|08. Her next WBBL appearance came two years later, when she was signed on a one-year deal by the Perth Scorchers ahead of WBBL|10.

In the WNCL, Leeson signed a contract with the NSW Breakers ahead of the 2017–18 season, but had to wait until 2019 to make her debut.

She made the move to Canberra ahead of 2019-20 after signing a contract with the ACT Meteors.

Players.Name: Naomi Stalenberg
Players.Bio:
Stalenberg started her career with NSW, making her debut against Tasmania in the 2013-14 season.

The allrounder went on to become a regular in the Breakers team, and signed with the Thunder for the first season of the WBBL.

She made her T20 debut for Australia against India in 2016, in what would be her only appearance in the green and gold. Stalenberg was selected for the 2018 tour to India but did not play a game.

Not offered a NSW contract in 2020, Stalenberg instead signed with Tasmania and shortly after penned a deal with the Hobart Hurricanes.

After four seasons in purple, Stalenberg was on the move once again, joining the Renegades for their title-winning WBBL|10 campaign.

Players.Name: Dani Gibson
Players.Bio:
A pace-bowling allrounder who debuted at Edgbaston during the T20I leg of the 2023 Ashes, Gibson has since secured her spot in England’s best XI in the shortest format.

She also proved an excellent addition to the Adelaide Strikers squad in WBBL|09, helping the club reach a second consecutive final.

Melbourne Stars leapt at the chance to draft Gibson ahead of WBBL|11 as she found her second Big Bash home.

Players.Name: Georgia Prestwidge
Players.Bio:
Georgia Prestwidge comes from right cricketing stock – her father is Queensland allrounder and current Australia assistant coach Scott and the sister of Jack and Will.

Prestwidge debuted for Queensland in October 2014, and at the end of the 2015–16 season, she was named the Queensland Fire Youth Player of the Year.

Prestwidge made her the Brisbane Heat debut in December 2016 against the Sydney Sixers.

She decided to make a move south to the Melbourne Renegades ahead of WBBL|08 and a year later, signed a state contract with Victoria.

In 2025, she made the switch to Melbourne Stars for WBBL|11.

Players.Name: Rhys McKenna
Players.Bio:
Rhys McKenna is a highly talented fast bowler who can generate swing and is an excellent fielder.

McKenna captained Victoria Country to the grand final of the 2022 Under-19 National Championships and was subsequently named captain of the Australian Under-19 T20 World Cup squad in early 2023.

The fast-bowling allrounder signed her first WBBL contract with the Melbourne Stars in 2021.

McKenna showed off her potential with the bat in WBBL|10, when she hammered a half-century off just 21 balls.

Players.Name: Kim Garth
Players.Bio:
Kim Garth holds a unique claim to fame, as the only woman to have played international cricket for both Ireland and Australia.

Born in Dublin to parents who both played cricket for Ireland, Garth made her debut when she was just 14 years old and featured in three World Cups for Ireland before making a call in 2020 that would change her life.

Having had a taste of life in Australia through stints in the WBBL - where she played for Sydney Sixers as an associate rookie before earning full contracts with Perth Scorchers and later, Melbourne Stars - Garth decided to walk away from Ireland and instead pursue the chance to be a full-time cricketer via a Victorian contract.

She became an Australian permanent resident in 2022, allowing her the chance to play in the WBBL as a local, and later the same year became eligible to play for Australia.

National selectors jumped at the chance to pick the right-arm pace bowler, including her in their T20 squad to tour India in December 2022, where she debuted in the opening game.

Her first Australian one-day call-up shortly followed for the January 2023 home series against Pakistan, and she made her Test debut against England five months later.

Players.Name: Sophie Day
Players.Bio:
Sophie Day continues to grow in stature having become a mainstay of the Stars and Victoria line-ups since making her debut in WBBL|06.

The left arm orthodox spinner was a latecomer to cricket and originally played hockey growing up, but has thrived since impressing scouts with her performances in Premier cricket.

Day is also a talented young artist having completed a Fine Arts degree and had her art exhibition ‘The Art of Cricket’ displayed at Cricket Victoria.

The spinner enjoyed a breakout season in WBBL|09, finishing as the BKT Golden Arm and claiming a place in the Team of the Tournament.

A call-up for the Australia A three-day game followed in early 2024, followed by representative honours against England A in 2025.

Players.Name: Phoebe Litchfield
Players.Bio:
Phoebe Litchfield was earmarked as a future Australian player early in her teenage years, and she first caught the eyes of fans when one of her net sessions with New South Wales went viral in 2019.

That same year she debuted for Sydney Thunder aged 16, becoming the youngest player to score a WBBL half-century in just her second match.

Her graduation from high school was quickly followed by her first Australia A outing against England, and her first preseason as a full-time cricketer quickly reaped rewards as Litchfield hit her first WNCL century for NSW in October 2022, and followed that with her best season to date for Sydney Thunder.

The left-hander was called into her first Australia T20I squad for the December 2022 tour of India, making her debut in the second match of the series, before being promoted to opener in place of an injured Alyssa Healy for the final game of the series.

Her first ODI call-up promptly followed for the 2023 home series against Pakistan, and she made her Test debut against England at Trent Bridge in June the same year.

Litchfield hit her first ODI century against Ireland a month later and her standout first 12 months of international cricket was rewarded when she was named the ICC's Emerging Cricketer of the Year for 2023.

Now a mainstay for Australia across all formats, Litchfield's leadership qualities were also recognised when she was named Sydney Thunder captain ahead of WBBL|10.

Players.Name: Georgia Voll
Players.Bio:
Identified early as a future Australia player, Toowoomba-raised Georgia Voll signed to the Brisbane Heat when she was just 16 years old.

She made her Queensland debut in February 2020, and played her first game for the Heat later the same year.

A classy and versatile top-to-middle-order batter, Voll also bowls handy spin.

She hit her first WNCL century in 2022 and followed up with two more in the 2023-24 season to help Queensland reach the WNCL final.

In January 2022, Voll was named in Australia's A squad for their series against England A, with the matches being played alongside the Women's Ashes.

She moved to the Sydney Thunder for the 2024 WBBL|10 season, a breakout campaign that saw her called up to open the batting for Australia in a home ODI series against India.

Voll repaid the faith of selectors when she hit a century in just her second ODI, and she would go on to make her T20I and Test debuts a month later during the 2025 Ashes. Her first full CA contract followed shortly after.

Those performances caught the eye of international competitions, with Voll subsequently picked up in the WPL and The Hundred. 

The talented athlete has also played rugby league, representing the Queensland women's under-18 rugby league team before switching her sole focus to cricket.

Players.Name: Anika Learoyd
Players.Bio:
A right-handed batter, Anika Learoyd is a proud Gumbaynggirr woman who made her Sydney Thunder debut during WBBL|06 in 2020, and her NSW Breakers debut in February 2021.

Learoyd took her game to new levels during the 2024-25 summer, dominating for NSW at No.3 and playing an increasingly important role for the Thunder. Those performances resulted in call-ups for Australia A.

Players.Name: Heather Knight
Players.DidyouKnow: In 2016, she became the first female cricketer to score a half-century and take a 5-wicket haul in an ODI innings.
Players.Bio:
From turning down an offer to study at the Cambridge University to becoming one of her England's most accomplished female cricketers today, Heather Knight's career has had many incredible highlights.

The allrounder initially started off as a batsman at the domestic level, playing for the Devon county team. Knight made her WODI debut in March 2010 against India, followed by her WT20I debut later that year. Early in 2011, she played her maiden Test at Sydney against Australia.

Beyond her consistent contributions with the bat and ball, Knight's captaincy has been a true standout - she led her side to the 2017 Women's Cricket World Cup title. Unsurprisingly and deservedly so, she was named as one of the five Wisden Cricketers of the Year in 2018.

Heather Knight has also made her presence felt in the WBBL, as part of the Hobart Hurricanes - both as player and captain.

Players.Name: Tahlia Wilson
Players.Bio:
Tahlia Wilson made her Big Bash debut in WBBL|04 playing for the Sydney Sixers while she was still in high school, earning her first NSW contract around the same time as she chose to pursue cricket over hockey.

The next season Wilson made the switch to the Sydney Thunder, becoming a core member of the top-order.

The wicketkeeper-batter has represented Australia's Under-19s and Australia A and in October 2022, scored her first WNCL century for NSW.

In 2023-24, Wilson created a new world record when she became the first woman to score a century and execute six dismissals in a List A match.

The following season, Wilson's excellent form saw her awarded the WNCL's player of the tournament during NSW's title-winning campaign. 

In March 2026, Wilson made her ODI debut against West Indies in St Kitts, filling in for an injured Beth Mooney, and was named as the travelling reserve in Australia's T20 World Cup squad for that year's tournament.

Players.Name: Laura Harris
Players.Bio:
Laura Harris, better known as 'Larris', is a powerful middle-order batter who has become a staple in the Brisbane Heat and Queensland Fire batting line-ups alongside her sister Grace.

Growing up in Ipswich, Laura tried out any sport she could including rugby league, soccer and cricket.

Laura loved playing club and school cricket growing up but decided to follow a career in nursing.

After a few years of working in the emergency department at Logan Hospital, Laura picked up a bat again, which rapidly catapulted her into a professional sporting career with the Queensland Fire and Brisbane Heat.

An excitement machine with bat in hand, Harris’s reputation has seen her pick up T20 gigs in leagues around the world, becoming one of the game’s cult heroes.

In late 2024, she shocked the Big Bash by switching allegiances from the Heat to the Thunder for WBBL|11.

Players.Name: Nadine de Klerk
Players.DidyouKnow: In September 2019, de Klerk was named in the F van der Merwe XI for the inaugural edition of the Women's T20 Super League.
Players.Bio:
Nadine de Klerk has been a part of the Northerns since she was 13, later also named as one of the Women's National Academy intake for 2019.

De Klerk made her international debut in an ODI against India in May 2017, followed by her T20I debut less than a year later.

The allrounder was captain of the South Africa Emerging Players squad during their home series against Bangladesh in 2019.

She was also included in South Africa's squad for the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2020, and produced a breakthrough performance in the semi-final at the SCG that saw the Proteas almost topple Australia.

That earned de Klerk her first taste of the WBBL with Brisbane Heat the same year, and in 2024, she confirmed she would return to the club, penning a two-year deal.

Players.Name: Jemma Barsby
Players.DidyouKnow: She has the rare talent of being able to bowl with both hands
Players.Bio:
Allrounder Jemma Barsby is an incredibly gifted cricketer who can bowl right or left-handed.

A dhampionship player with the Brisbane Heat in WBBL|04, Barsby became a Striker in WBBL|07 following two seasons in the west with Perth.

She made an immediate impact in her first season in blue, boasting the second-best bowling economy amongst her teammates and was one of only four Strikers to deliver a maiden over through her nine matches of WBBL|07.

A leader and inspiration to teammates on and off the pitch, Jemma was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis as a 19-year-old and continues to serve as an ambassador for several charities as a fine role model for many aspiring athletes.

She is also the daughter of former Queensland batsman and coach Trevor Barsby and made her Women’s National Cricket League debut for Queensland in the 2010-11 season at the age of 15. 

These days, she captains South Australia while plying her trade in the WBBL for Adelaide Strikers.

Players.Name: Nicola Hancock
Players.DidyouKnow: Hancock was part of the Shooting Stars squad for a tour of Dubai in 2015
Players.Bio:
Nicola Hancock was born and raised in Melbourne, but Queensland have now claimed her as their own after she joined both the Brisbane Heat and Queensland Fire.

The allrounder began her career as part of the Victorian under-15 squad, and her determination and drive saw her included in not only the Victorian under-18 side, but also the Shooting Stars during their 2015 tour of Dubai.

Having previously played for Hobart Hurricanes and the Melbourne Stars, Hanock is now a core member of the Heat XI since signing with the club ahead of WBBL|06.

On the state side of things, she made the move to the Fire after previously playing for Victoria and ACT Meteors.

When she is not playing cricket, she's busy renovating her home in Boondall, playing with her Bull Arab pup Hansen, and spending as much time as she can outdoors enjoying day trips to Mooloolaba and the Redcliffe Markets on a Sunday.

She also runs her own personal training business.

Players.Name: Sam Bates
Players.DidyouKnow: Bates started her career as a fast bowler
Players.Bio:
Sam Bates grew up in Newcastle and was originally a fast bowler, before she was encouraged to take up spin after undergoing a knee reconstruction due to a soccer training accident when she was 16.

The left-arm orthodox spinner toured Dubai in 2015 with the Shooting Stars and after joining the Sydney Thunder ahead of WBBL|01, claimed the club’s first-ever WBBL wicket.

Bates has remained loyal in lime green across the decade since, leading the club’s spin attack.

But she has moved around the country throughout that time, departing the ACT Meteors after more than a decade contracted to the state and signing with Tasmania for the 2019-20 WNCL season.

Then, in 2021, she relocated to Melbourne after earning a state contract with Victoria.

An injury plagued 2023-24 summer left Bates' future in limbo as she parted ways with Victoria, but a lifeline offered by NSW saw the spinner train with the Breakers during the preseason.

She made a long-awaited debut for her state of birth at the start of the 2024-25 WNCL season, and carried that form into the WBBL where she had a dominant season for the Thunder.
